resumo: Organized assets, a protected family and a business prepared for the next generation.
servicos: Gifts and gifts with reserved usufruct
Prenuptial agreements and changes to the marital property regime
Partners’ agreements and succession in the family business

assuntos.faz: We identify which assets exist, in whose name they are held and what would happen to them today, without any planning.
We assess whether it makes sense: the cost of setting it up and maintaining it, compared with what is actually saved.
We bring forward the transfer of assets while the donor keeps their use and income for life.
We record the person’s wishes on what happens to their assets, respecting the share reserved by law for the forced heirs.
We draft prenuptial agreements and handle changes to the marital property regime, taking into account the effects on succession.
We set out in a partners’ agreement who manages the business and how heirs join the company, while everyone is in agreement.
We calculate the tax on each alternative before the decision, and not when there is no longer a choice.
We handle it at a notary’s office when there is consensus and in court when there is not.

corpo: Estate and succession planning means deciding during your lifetime what will happen to your assets, instead of leaving that decision to the law and the courts. It is a preventive area: much of what it resolves would otherwise become, later on, a lengthy probate, a higher tax than necessary or a family conflict.

Gifts with reserved usufruct, wills, prenuptial agreements, changes to the marital property regime and family holding companies are instruments for organizing the transfer, defining who manages each asset and reducing the risk of litigation. There is no model that suits everyone. Each instrument has its own cost, tax effect and legal limits, and the choice depends on the makeup of the assets and of the family.

Half of the estate is reserved by law for the forced heirs (descendants, ascendants and spouse). This is the so-called legítima (forced share), and no will or gift can set it aside. Planning organizes the transfer within this limit and decides freely on the other half.

The ITCMD, the state tax on inheritances and gifts, usually determines the timing and form of the transfer. With the tax reform, it must now be charged progressively: the higher the amount transferred, the higher the rate. Planning is not about avoiding tax. It is about knowing the cost of each path before choosing.

In a family business, succession is also a corporate matter. The partners’ agreement, the rules for heirs joining the company and the definition of who will manage the business prevent the death of a partner from paralyzing the company. These are clauses that must be written while there is consensus.

When there was no planning, or to complete what was planned, probate (inventário) transfers the assets of the deceased to the heirs. When there is consensus, it can be done at a notary’s office, by public deed, which is usually much faster. Since CNJ (National Council of Justice) Resolution 571/2024, this is possible in some cases even when there is a will or an heir who is a minor, subject to specific conditions. When there is disagreement, the path is the courts.

The work begins with an assessment: which assets exist, in whose name, with what debts and which people are involved. Before any step, we present the alternatives, what each one requires and how much it costs. We do not promise results, because the outcome of a proceeding does not depend on the lawyer alone.
We serve clients throughout Brazil online and in person in Maringá (Paraná).

perguntas.pergunta: What is estate and succession planning?
perguntas.resposta: It is organizing, during your lifetime, how your assets will be managed and passed on to your heirs. Instead of letting the law and the probate proceeding define everything later, the person decides, within legal limits, who gets what, who manages the assets and when the transfer takes place. The goal is to reduce costs, time and the risk of family conflict.

perguntas.pergunta: Is succession planning only for people with large estates?
perguntas.resposta: No. A family with a single property can also face a lengthy probate or a disagreement among heirs. What changes with the size of the estate are the appropriate instruments: in some cases a will or a gift is enough. In others, a more complex structure, such as a holding company, makes sense.

perguntas.pergunta: If I plan, will I still need probate?
perguntas.resposta: It depends on the instrument chosen. Assets given during one’s lifetime or transferred to a holding company are no longer part of the probate, because they no longer belong to the person when they die. A will, on the other hand, does not dispense with probate: it guides the division, but the assets still need to go through probate.

perguntas.pergunta: Can I leave my assets to whomever I want?
perguntas.resposta: Partly. Anyone who has forced heirs (children and other descendants, parents and other ascendants, and spouse) must reserve half of their estate for them, the so-called legítima (forced share). The person may freely dispose of the other half, by will or gift, in favor of any person or institution.

perguntas.pergunta: Is it worth setting up a family holding company?
perguntas.resposta: For some estates, yes. For others, no. A holding company can make it easier to manage the assets and handle succession, but it has setup and maintenance costs, accounting obligations and its own taxation. The ITBI (municipal tax on property transfers) immunity on transferring properties into the holding company also has limits. That is why the decision should come after comparing the cost of the structure with what it actually saves.

perguntas.pergunta: What is a gift with reserved usufruct?
perguntas.resposta: It is a gift in which the person transfers ownership of the asset to the heirs but keeps for themselves the right to use it and receive its income for life. Upon death, the usufruct ends and the heirs acquire full ownership, without the asset having to go through probate. The gift may include clauses that protect the assets, such as one providing that the asset does not become shared property with the heir’s spouse.

perguntas.pergunta: Is planning a way to avoid paying tax?
perguntas.resposta: No. The transfer of assets, whether by inheritance or by gift, is subject to the ITCMD, a state tax. What planning allows is knowing the cost of each alternative and choosing the timing and form of the transfer in an informed way. With the tax reform, the ITCMD now must have progressive rates, which makes this analysis even more important.

perguntas.pergunta: Can probate be done at a notary’s office?
perguntas.resposta: Yes, when the heirs agree on the division. Probate at a notary’s office, done by public deed and with the participation of a lawyer, is usually much faster than probate in court. Since 2024, it has been possible in some cases even when there is a will or an heir who is a minor, provided specific conditions are met. If the heirs disagree, the path is the courts.

perguntas.pergunta: Is there a deadline to open probate?
perguntas.resposta: Yes. The law provides that probate must be opened within two months of the death. Missing the deadline does not prevent it from being done later, but many states charge a penalty on the ITCMD when the deadline is not met. Until probate is concluded, the heirs cannot sell or transfer the assets normally.

perguntas.pergunta: Does the marital property regime affect inheritance?
perguntas.resposta: Yes, a great deal. Depending on the regime, the spouse may be entitled to their half of the common property (meação), which already belongs to them, to an inheritance share, or to both, including in competition with the children. In a stable union (união estável), the partner has the same inheritance rights as a spouse. That is why choosing or changing the marital property regime, and the prenuptial agreement, are part of succession planning.
